title: Keep the front door and the ledger honest at the boundary
goal: Two advisories, neither a gate, because prose and evidence forced by a check become rubber stamps. (1) A task that changes the CLI surface but not README.md leaves the front door describing a tool that no longer exists: warn at push (Workflow Compliance) when the pushed range touches src/cli/ without touching README.md, and prove the warning fires and stays silent otherwise. (2) Evidence is a convention: the ledger is what ranks providers by recorded outcomes, so an entry minted to satisfy a check is noise. Prompt once at close - only when the task's claim reserved crates/ and no entry names the task - that if it changed a design decision or produced a measurement it should be recorded, and say plainly that a rubber-stamp entry is worse than none.
